steps.title: A fair start
steps.body: Defenders have to guess when the ball will be snapped. If blockers could ==move early==, they'd get an unfair head start on every play.

steps.title: Set means set
steps.body: Before the snap, offensive linemen must hold ==completely still== for a full second. Any ==sudden move== that looks like the start of the play is a false start.
steps.note: Ref signal: forearms rolled over each other in front of the body.

steps.title: The flinch
steps.body: The tackle jerks his shoulders a split second early. The ball never moved, but the flag comes out: that ==flinch== is a false start.

steps.title: Legal motion
steps.body: One player, usually a receiver, may move ==sideways or backward== before the snap. It's legal as long as he's ==not moving forward== when the ball is snapped.

steps.title: The hard count
steps.body: Quarterbacks bark a loud fake count to ==draw the defense offside==. If a defender jumps into the neutral zone, the foul is on ==the defense== instead.

steps.title: Five yards back
steps.body: A false start is a ==dead-ball foul==: the play never happens. The offense loses ==5 yards== and replays the down.

options: The center snapped it too early
The right tackle moved before the snap
Too many players on the field
steps.explain: The ball never moved, but the right tackle flinched out of his stance. That's a false start: 5 yards, replay the down.

steps.prompt: What happens after a false start?
options: Automatic first down for the defense
steps.explain: The play is dead before it starts. The offense moves back 5 yards and runs the same down again.
